newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday July 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday July 9.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Finance minister Vincenzo Visco said he agreed with Bank of Italy Governor's stand on the excessive fiscal burden weighing on the economy but added that prime minister Romano Prodi was also right to say it was too early to cut taxes (all).

* Giorgio Fossa, head of industrialists' organisation Confindustria, said the long-awaited economic upturn in Italy had not appeared yet and financial markets were still waiting for clear signs of economic recovery. Fossa also said tax burden ought to be reduced and labour market should be more flexible (all).

* Centre-right opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi, whose Mediaset company operates three national stations, said he was ready to force a confidence vote on a bill he fears could hurt private broadcasters. Berlusconi's Forza Italia later found a compromise with centre-left government (all).

* A report by national statistics institute Istat showed Italy had a 4.534 trillion lire trade surplus with non-European countries in May against 3.628 trillion in April and 4.770 trillion in May 1996. Istat said May figures showing an increase in both imports and exports suggested that firms believe an economic recovery is on the way (Sole 24 Ore).

* Shares in Istituto San Paolo di Torino rose over five percent to new year's highs of 14,100 lire per share on the Milan bourse, boosted by press talk about plans of the new management of Italy's largest commercial bank following its May public share placement (all).
* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said the recent fall in long-term Italian bond spread should soon be followed by a similar reduction in short-term spreads (all).

* Gaetano Galia, managing director of Aereoporti di Roma - the first Italian airport company to be privatised - said the group expects to be listed on the Milan bourse on July 24 or 25. Galia also said the group expects to see increased profitability with business continuing to grow in coming years (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
